reviewerStanding: INDEPENDENT of the subject's authorship: I did not author v1, v2, v3 or v4. I DID author both the v2 and the v3 verdicts. That is disclosed rather than treated as disqualifying, and it carries a specific and now-compounding risk: a reviewer checking whether an artifact complied with their own two verdicts is prone both to confirmation and to its opposite - defending a prior blocker past the harm it was raised against. Both were guarded. Every repair below was re-measured from primary sources rather than compared against my verdicts' text, and the central judgment in this review is a decision NOT to re-raise my own v3 blocker at one remove, with the distinguishing principle stated explicitly at advisory A1 so a coordinator can overrule it.

verdictBasis.statement: ACCEPT WITH ADVISORIES. The v3 blocker is discharged completely and accurately: all nine v2-verdict findings now carry dispositions, the logged ID set matches the verdict's ID set exactly with no omission and no invention, and the five recorded as REPAIRED were genuinely repaired while the four recorded as CARRIED are genuinely still open. Every one of the prompt's five verification items passes. No blocker survives and none is newly raised.
verdictBasis.whatChanged: The v3->v4 diff is 16 pointers: 8 added, 0 removed, 8 changed. Every one is accounting. No design text was touched, no measurement was re-opened, and no repaired text was disturbed. This is the narrowest generation in the chain and it does exactly what its task specified.
verdictBasis.theBlockerIsGone: v3 was rejected because it named a verdict at digest in its header and then discharged it invisibly - five findings repaired with no record, four dropped with no word. v4 adds /repairLog/predecessorVerdictFindings with an entry per finding, lists the v2 verdict at /appliesFindingsOf/verdicts, extends the header exclusion to /artifact, records the v3 B1 repair at /repairLog/v3ReviewFinding, and adds /v4AuthoringWindow. Nothing is waived and nothing is silently dropped.
verdictBasis.whyNotREJECT: The one candidate for a fresh blocker is that v4 logs only one of the v3 verdict's five findings by ID. I examined it closely and it does not reach blocker grade, because ALL FIVE were actually acted on and every action is visible in v4's bytes: /artifact was added to the exclusion (v3-A1), /v4AuthoringWindow was created (v3-A2), the date correction is recorded in the generationNote (v3-A3), and the four carried v2 advisories now have CARRIED dispositions (v3-A4). The v3 blocker was a WAIVER - findings that received neither action nor record. What remains here is an INDEXING gap - actions performed and recorded, but not keyed to the verdict IDs that prompted them. That is a real distinction, not a softening, and it is the line between the two verdicts. Re-raising the blocker for an indexing gap after the waiver it targeted has been cured would apply the rule past the harm it exists to prevent, and would block a candidate that has no substantive defect on bookkeeping about bookkeeping.
verdictBasis.whyNotPlainACCEPT: Six advisories are live, one of which (A2) is an accuracy defect inside the new accounting block itself - the A5 disposition's stated reason misdescribes the finding it disposes of. In a corpus where the record is the deliverable, a misdescribed finding in a freshly added record is worth naming even though the disposition attached to it is correct.
verdictBasis.acceptGate: Nothing here blocks coordinator disposition of DR-114 on the merits. Every advisory is a one-line or one-block correction, none requires a design change, a new measurement campaign, or the actor decision.
verdictBasis.scoringNote: Scored by FINDING-SET against v4's bytes. No checker was run.

reviewSummary: ACCEPT WITH ADVISORIES. v3's sole blocker is discharged completely and, more importantly, accurately. All nine v2-verdict findings now carry dispositions; the logged ID set matches the verdict's ID set exactly in both directions, with nothing omitted and nothing invented; and I verified the labels rather than merely counting them - the five marked REPAIRED were genuinely repaired and the four marked CARRIED are genuinely still open. The v2 verdict is listed at appliesFindingsOf with a correct standing, the header exclusion now names /artifact so a full v1-to-v4 diff returns zero unaccounted pointers where v3 returned one, and v4 volunteered two things no blocker required: a build-window record and a note recording v3's date correction. All five mandated checks pass. Every recited count recomputed and replicates, including the five-member counts block and the two verdict standings. All 255 precisely-delimited quotations resolve exactly, with zero case divergences. The actor question is untouched - actorMismatch is byte-identical to v3's in its entirety - and the reserved binding points remain unpopulated. No D9 or exit value is minted. Tokens stay confined at 29 occurrences with none outside. The generation is 16 pointers wide and touches nothing but accounting. Six advisories are live. The one a coordinator should look at first is that v4 logs only one of the v3 verdict's five findings by ID; I examined that closely as a candidate blocker and concluded it is not one, because all five were actually acted on and every action is visible in the bytes. The v3 blocker was a waiver - findings receiving neither action nor record; what remains is an indexing gap - actions performed and recorded but not keyed to the IDs that prompted them. That distinction is the whole of the difference between rejecting v3 and accepting v4, and it is stated plainly so it can be overruled. Adopting the general rule that each generation logs every finding of the verdict it answers would close the class permanently rather than one generation at a time.
